body: Here is one of the tallest seated Buddha statues in the world! There is a viewing platform at the foot of the statue, from where you can see the square in front of the temple, as well as the surrounding areas. Despite this, the temple is little known and little visited by tourists. The temple itself, which has a very unusual architecture and frescoes in the temple, was built in 1734.
title: Buddhist temple complex

body: Our 2nd excursion trip was a a boat trip in the mangroves and a visit to Kandhe Vihare temple. Charindu from Cherry Tours was our personal guide.We started the boat trip by exploring bats hanging casually from the trees. Further down we saw monkeys were we fed them various fruits which they absolutely loved. We also saw baby crocodiles,lizards , beautiful blue hummingbirds and various other birds. Our next part of the trip was to visit the Buddhist temple.Once you arrive you are greeted by an enormous statue of Buddha. You will find stalls selling flowers, fruits,incense which you can offer to the many gods inside.Once you climb the steps inside you are surrounded by many smaller temples which have beautiful statues and paintings.Charindu explained the different gods and local history of the place.Inside you will find many locals performing poojas, praying and finding spiritual solace.There is a large Bodhi tree and a house containing statues and paintings depicting the life of Buddha. This place is spiritually enriching and you can immerse yourself in the local culture. After we left the temple on tuk tuk just a few minutes away we saw an elephant owned by the temple. Overall this was a good local trip only 2-3 hours and highly recommend.Thanks to Cherry tours and Charindu +94 761337323 K. Patel
title: Mangrove boat and Kande Viharaya trip

body: Kande viharaya temple located at Aluthgama is another tourist attraction that you may get astound of the tourism of sri lanka. The name of this sacred place means ‘Mountain Temple. The temple gains most of its current fame, not from its historical elements; but from the gigantic Samdhi Buddha statue unveiled in 2006. This 48 m statue is the tallest Seated Buddha statue in the world. Kande Vihare has all the important features necessary for a major Buddhist Temple. These include the Stupa, Bo Tree, Relic Chamber, Image House, Sri Vishnu Temple and the four Great Temples.We visited the temple with Wasantha Tours and it was an amazing experience.

body: After a long day of sightseeing down along the southern coast, we were ready to head back to our resort on the beach. However our driver asked if we were interested in stopping here. And I'm really happy he did in the end. I had looked this place up before our trip and yet I totally forgot about it for some reason (and it's only a few minutes from where we're staying too). It was one of the spots that I didn't want to miss. If you're just passing through the area it's not far from the Colombo-Galle main road. The entrance way takes you up a hill (via tuk tuk) along a short road with short carved walls featuring the Korawak Gal (These area also on the steps leading up to the hill). We were greeted by a fat and loud chicken - most likely overjoyed that he wasn't on someone's plate. (Other chickens and animals on the grounds have found sanctuary here). We made a bee-line directly to the front of the statue. This Samadhi Buddha is enormous and one of the tallest sitting statues in the world. The light colors on Buddha stood out against the crisp blue afternoon sky and looked wonderful. (I'm posting photos). Don't forget to take your shoes off. We arrived close to 5 in the afternoon so the stones were warm - almost comforting. (There are some stray dogs so watch out for poop). Since we did not take the stairs up, we did not get to see the Thorana.After staring at the giant statue and checking out the stair case with the awesome Makara Korawakgala, I decided to walk around the bottom instead of up the stairs between the marble lions. The outside of the chamber below Buddha is lined with life-size figures of the kings of Sri Lanka including King Devanampiya Tissa - he was the man in charge when Buddhism came to Sri Lanka. Upon entering the image chamber I got another second wind. The air was nice and cool and the sight is impressive. Stairs leading up and down take you to different sections of the room. It's dark and yet the frescoes inside are so vibrant. Here you can see the Jataka tales that show Buddha in previous births teaching lessons while in various forms (man, animal, god, etc.) There are so many paintings inside, I wish there was a guide available to explain each one. This room is really peaceful. There were a couple of ladies sitting on the stairs talking quietly and discussing the images. I wish I could've understood what they were saying. Take your time and look at the art as well as the room as a whole.I think my group was done for the day. So I did not get to see the relic chamber, Bo tree (supposed to be 300+ years old!) or Devala. I kind of think I should've gone back for a second visit however there's another week of ancient places to visit yet to come!This is a working temple and place of worship. It is also free of charge. You can make a donation if you'd like. It was not crowded when we arrived and non-worshipers were welcome too.This could easily be a fast visit if you've got things to do or an extended one if you really want to look at the details and learn a bit more.
title: Be Happy and Free ...

body: I never have been really a temple-going person though I'm a Buddhist by birth.. However went there for the first time on one of my friend's persuasion to seek blessings. "Kande Viharaya" (temple on hillock) is renowned for its "Upulwan Devalaya"; a shrine dedicated to Lord Vishnu; among several other shrines situated inside the temple.I didn't feel like taking any pictures as it felt something divine and spiritual about the place as I entered. Therefore I focused solely on the purpose of my visit.However, I thought of writing this review after seeing few disappointed overseas tourists at the temple. My fellow overseas travelers please be advised that this is merely a place of worship for locals and therefore it would not exactly fit as a sightseeing attraction, unless you have any interests in understanding the local religion, beliefs and culture. Please do not fall into the recommendations of local tour guides/ tuk tuk drivers to avoid disappointments in your precious visit to Sri Lanka. It is true that this temple is very sacred for them, but for many of you it would be just another temple with Buddhist sculpture and paintings.
title: Place of Worship - No Sightseeing

body: Kande Viharaya is located in Aluthgama, about 15 mins drive from Bentota. The temple is not very difficult to locate and can be found easily with the help of the locals. The temple is little different and unique as it has a huge Buddha Statue in the front and an old Hindu temple at the back. The statue of the Buddha is magnificent. It's really huge and very beautiful. Such is the idol that it seems like the idol is touching the sky. There is also a museum depicting paintings of ancient times. The museum is life history of Buddha. There is no detail/board available in English through which you can understand the history of the huge Buddha statue and the temple. Nor is there anyone available whom you can ask. Behind the museum there is a hindu temple with many hindu deities.A must visit if you're in Bentota or around.

body: Great temple to visit away from the more crowded spots in Colombo, although it probably wouldn't make sense to come here all the way from Colombo just for this. Bentota/Beruwala are more local access points. Awe-inspiring statue of Buddha, best viewed from the base of a long stone stairway, but don't go up this way as you won't find a place to keep your footwear. Instead, walk up the driveway and enter from the front side. Also partake of the Dutch influence in the white building behind the main temple. Not enough English instructions for tourists and the museum was closed without any details on till when. Shopkeepers at the base of the temple (near the parking) don't speak or understand English, but will still try to fleece you unless you go with a local who speaks Sinhala. Temple Web-site is only in Sinhala.
title: Massive Buddha Statue in the Middle of Nowhere

body: We were taken there by one of the local drivers. It was my first experience of visiting a temple, so it was nice. You have to take off your shoes when you go there. But if it is hot, you have to look out for your feet not burning on hot ground. It was very interesting how locals respected and behaved in that place. You could see most of them carrying fruits designed beautifully in trays while going to the temple.
title: Good to visit

body: This temple is around 30-40 min drive from Beruwala off Colombo Galle highway. The statue is huge and stunning. One downside is whatever written there is in local language with no translation in english available
title: Huge Buddha Statue

body: The inside of the temple is very nicely decorated but dirty. Dog poop outside the door and you have to take your shoes off! Large Buddha was impressive. Elephant tied up too tight outside is sad to see and unnecessary.
title: Modern Temple

body: If you are in Aluthgama/ Benton area this is a place to visit. You will see a museum with history of Buddhism in beautiful art. A massive Buddha statue etc. Fully worth the trip up to the temple.
title: Visit to a sacred Temple in Aluthgama

body: this temple seems like it was built the ruins of a more ancient site. the stairway is intricately with all manner of interesting creatures icons. Really something to see.The temple itself is pretty modern.. The buddha statue a bit 'colourful' but inside many bright and colorful murals. Pity however is that nothing anywhere is translated into english.. thus you don't really get the value of the place. Suggest some advance reading before you go.
title: interesting although modern temple

body: Kande Viharaya is a very famous located in Aluthgama. There is a huge Buddha statue in the temple, which is the icon of the temple. You can visit the temple by train too. The temple has been around for many centuries and is one of the most sacred places in the province. Visiting the temple will take less than three hours. It is famous for the Vishnu Devalaya, which is considered to be very sacred. The temple also has a museum, which would take less than a hour to visit. The temple can be crowded during the Weekends and Poya days. It is too hot there in the afternoon, so if you planning a visit, plan to get there before 11 A.M. Overall, the temple is a very good place and is definitely worth a visit.
title: A must-visit within the limits of the Western Province

body: wonderful temple not far from Bentota. You can go all he way up with a car but it is much more interesting to park at the Marketplace and walk all the stairs to discover step by step the huge statue. Once you left your shoes you can visit freely the inner temple area and make pictures without flash. There is a lot of history to discover,painted and carved all over the entire walls with wonderful bright colours and very well maintained. Further backwards you can also freely visit the hindu temple and the temple with the stretched buddha. At the south side the Buddhist monk dwellings are situated. When we visited this temple we also could talk with the mahout and his elephant who were there. A fantastic place that you must have seen.
title: perfect temple on hidden place

body: The temple is located at Matugama area little away from the Colombo-Galle main road.It is famous for the huge sitting budhdha statue. The "Dewalaya" in the temple is also famous.
title: One Big Buddha Statue

body: Close to the main road and a beautiful place to visit. One of the largest temples in Aluthgama area.
title: Calm and peaceful

body: We visited this temple in the evening as suggested by our driver/guide. It is a very nice temple with a huge Buddha statue (160ft). There is also a nice stupa and many Hindu gods like Vishnu and Murugan can be seen in this temple. The temple is well maintained and worth visiting when in Srilanka. We were told that Colombo was only 70 Kms. away from the temple.
title: A Nice Temple

body: We visited the big budda in aluthgama early evening in October. We chose this time as we were advised that the heat would be lesser and the crowds of tourists less too. We were staying at the centara and took a tuk tuk up there. Our driver (who we'd used before) spike fab English and took us around the sights, explaining what different ceremonies were occurring and the concepts of the Buddhist faith. It was very informative and we felt welcome and not an interesting in people religious endeavours which is sometimes a concern of mine when poking around churches etc. This temple is very alive and part of a faith which is integral to approx 70% of the Sri Lankan residents. Wasn't too impressed with princess the elephants area though. She is a bit of a forlorn distressed spectacle. 😕
title: Early evening trip

body: Kande viharaya off Aluthgama is unique temple that saved life of thousand during tsunami in 2006.Situated on a small hill with a picturesque Buddha statue this temple being visited by many devotees.
title: Above the rest

body: Very nice temple although not that old has a great feel about it . The buddah is huge and apparently when out at sea it appears to be floating in mid air .
title: Biggest sitting buddah

body: Visited here on our driver's recommendation. It has a big buddha statue and is a famous temple in this part of the country.Lots of local people visit the temple. It was really hot hot noon when we visited here. I suggest visit early morning or evenings.
title: A religious place worth a visit

body: Visited this temple before Sri Lanka.. And was defiantly worth a visit! If visiting on a weekend be aware lots of locals will be there too and it can be very busy! Visit during a weekday if possible! The massive Buddha is the largest Buddha is Asia! It is massive! You can get some beautiful photos.Inside the Buddha temple is very interesting it has beautiful pictures and amazing colours everywhere! Even the ceilings are painted. One section of the temple has been hand painted and is devoted to the tsunami that happened in 2004! Very interesting to look at! If you have chance go and visit the old temple it's very different to the new temple!!This temple is beautiful and very hidden in Aluthgama.. I only heard about this temple by word of mouth!!
title: Must see!!

body: the place i like visit most in aluthgama. it has huge Buddhas statue and you can see a fantastic view from there..there got elephant tooo
title: big landmark of western cost...

body: This temple is well worth a visit, just a short Tuktuk ride from Aluthgama centre. The paintings are lovely, the huge mural remembering the tsunami is really sad. And the Big Bhudda is really BIG! It is a real surprise finding this lovely temple in a small town like Aluthgama, a busy place of worship, the locals are very friendly and welcoming.
title: Stunning temple

body: As we were staying in The Palms in Beruwala, we decided to take a day trip and check out the nearby surroundings in a hired car. Kande Viharaya Temple was one of attractions we visited as we were told it is the tallest sitting Buddha statue in the world. This statue is in a place called Aluthgama. We had to park our car at some distance and then walk to the temple. As is usual outside the temple there were many fruit and flower sellers. Since we were there before noon, luckily it was not crowded. We were told it gets lots of visitors on the weekends. We got a full picture of the Buddha Statue from the road where our car was parked.
title: Impressive

body: This was quite a spectacular attraction, however thoroughly spoilt for us by the elephant outside, chained up so he could barely move, to earn money from feeding and photos.
title: Interesting, but......

body: One of the largest temples in the area, which can get quite crowded on full moon poya days. Otherwise it is nice and peaceful place to stroll around and take a look at the various stories in picture form within the Buddha statue.
title: Peaceful

body: We have visited many temples in Sri Lanka and this was defintely one of my favourites. The temple is calm and beautiful and the buddha statue is truly breath taking both from the outside and within. If you are interested in Buddhism check out the bookshop that offers some very good value english books on buddhism. I liked this temple so much, that i visited twice in 2days.
title: Do not miss!

body: Very peaceful place. A lot of local hindu and buddists people are here. Unusial alliance of hindu and buddistsreligions in the one temple. Very very spiritual place. Don't miss it.
title: Don't miss it

body: We visited this temple as we were told that it is a very holy one. There is a giant Buddha statue outside and one has to take care not to have one's back towards the statue while taking a snap, per the people there. It is famous for its Vishnu temple.One can sit in the temple inside for a few moments and experience the tranquility.There is a museum next to the temple which is nothing great.
title: Good experience

body: A nice temple to see on your way down south of the country. has a huge Buddha statue in the temple which is a specialty of the temple. The temple has an elephant in the location as well..
title: Beautiful big Buddha Statue

body: With the help of our amazing Guide Jimi (+94 77 139 4859) we visited this temple and had a chance to get introduced to the religious culture . You can take as many pictures as you like inside the temple and outside next to the amazing elephant. There is a huge Budha statue outside , so if you want to take a picture to show it all , better take your picture before your reach the temple while you are driving towards it .
title: A must See

body: Famous for its Vishnu devale , locals go there for their spiritual rites and Buddhist rituals. It is avery old .Now it is adorned with a huge statue of load Buddha which was built few years ago. There is a little museum displaying various things among history of the temple.
title: Famous for its Vishnu devale

body: The temple is located few kilometres inland from the main road which runs from Colombo to Matara. If you do not have a vehicle better to hire a Tuk Tuk. The temple has got huge Buddha statue and also Kovil attached to the temple. The Kovil structure is similar to a church and it was started to build as a church but later converted to a temple.
title: Buddhist religious lactation with magnificent Buddha statue

body: Kande viharaya Aluthgama is just a few hundred meters from the Beruwala tourist Hotels. its walking distance. There are NO entrance fees to this temple and sign boards installed clearly states this and also NO GUIDES. this is in contrast to other Temples like some in Colombo where foreigners are charged.
title: A temple worth a visit

body: easy tuk tuk ride to temple with very tall Buddah-well worth it for the paintings inside and views from the hill its on.
title: 20 mins from Benota and Beruwala

body: Large Buddha and 2 elephants ( chained up) colourful temple .inside. only a short walk/tuk tuk ride from club bentota
title: local temple with elephants

body: With the aid of a guide (taxi driver) an interesting introduction to Buddhist religion. But the Buddha and the interior of the temple and other building are absolutely stunning. Apart from a requirement to maintain respectful dress and remove shoes, the visitor is at liberty to talk, photograph and walk around without any fear of disturbing those at prayer or involved in other rituals - they are completely unfazed by tourists.
title: Stunning - not to be missed

body: This is a good place if you like to visit a place of worship.Remeber to be properly attired when visiting. Females should not wear sleeveless tops and no shot skirts or shorts.
title: A Buddhist Temple together with a Hindu shrine

body: Beautiful scenic view. remarkable place in Buddhism. good to do meditation also.just few hour drive from aluthgama city. It is situated in top of mountain.
title: Very beautiful

body: Not a must see place. But if you have time. Just stroll around that place. Its more like a spiritual place than a sight seeing place. As couples i would rather suggest spend more time with your partner doing water sports in Bentota.
title: Good place.

body: . Just a revelation with respect to Buddhism. The New Year meant is was especially active. Worth having your taxi driver/guide show you everything otherwise you could miss out. Easy to feel inhibited but those who are praying or making offerings are not at all put out by the intrusion of tourists.
title: An absolute must

body: This tallest Buddha temple was in very pleasant surroundings. Although the ground was too hot even in October to be bare feet, it was great to walk around it. I felt so small in front of this Great Mahatama Buddha Statue. The views around the area were great from the top. The temple underneath the statue was marvellous. It was decorated with beautiful pictures, stories and paintings of Gods and Goddesses etc. There was some rennovation work going on inside, so the top floor was closed to the public. Overall a great outing, well worth a visit.
title: Magnificent Giant Buddha Statue

body: it is few minutes walk from the main road. better to walk to the temple in the evening. ladys and men should dress something below than there knees . white is prefers. and there are two elepants in the temple. we spent like one hour in the temple and it was a nice time. remember to visit the temple on a week day and in the evening . because if you go there on a weekend then there are lots of local crowd. and you dont have to pay for anything in the temple. remember to buy some flowers from the poor people who sells and offer it in the temple.
title: nice temple and big buddha statue

body: Lots to see and do on the way to Kande, including tea plantations, monkeys, waterfalls, botanic gardens, herbal remedies including massage, very nice! A traditional dance evening followed by a visit to the Temple
title: tour

body: I have visited this temple a few times and i think its lovely. A huge Buddah is the first thing you see when approaching. It is allways a busy place with temple goers arriving with alms etc. Just before the temple is a busy fruit market where you can buy fruit and flowers as offerings. Great for some good photos. Looking around the temple is great with its decorated tree. Behind the temple is the buddhist students living quaters and school and they really dont mind you wandering in and seeing the temples 2 elephants. Just a really nice place...
title: love this place!!
Commercialized
body: Liked the Giant Buddha Statue. Disliked very much the commercialization of the temple. Quite contrast to the Buddhists principles a lot of prominence is given for 'Devala' for worshiping numerous Gods. There were many stations for collecting money from the people compared to the area of worship. even the elephant is used as a source of income

title: club hotel bentota & spa
body: nothing to dislike a nice resort with lovely Sri Lankan people
